sense: a way in; the right or chance to reach or use

terms.gloss: access, approach; the right to approach
evidence: Gell. 16.5.3: per quem ā viā aditus accessusque ad aedīs est

terms.gloss: admission to see an important person, an audience
evidence: Sen. Ben. 6.33.4: prīmae et secundae admissiōnēs (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. available: access (to an important or busy person)
Ter. Ph. 113: sibi ut ejus faciat cōpiam

phrases.latin: locum ante jānuam domūs vacuum, per quem ā viā aditus accessusque ad aedīs est
phrases.english: the open space in front of the door of a house, through which there is access from the street to the house

phrases.latin: dum furor in cursū est, currentī cēde furōrī; difficilēs aditūs impetus omnis habet
phrases.english: while the rage is running, give way to it as it runs: every outburst is hard to get near

sources: Lewis & Short: aditus · Lewis & Short: accessus · Lewis & Short: admissio · Lewis & Short: copia
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. available: access (to an important or busy person).
